chunks: From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, regarding what I know, from Abu Ali al-Hadda', from Hariz, from Hariz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: 'The furthest the servant can be from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is when he is not concerned except for his belly and his private part.'

key_terms.فَرْجُهُ: His private part (referring to sexual desire)

ai.seo_question: What is the furthest distance a servant can be from Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the maximum spiritual distance from Allah as occurring when a servant’s primary preoccupation is limited to their belly and private part, a concept central to Shia asceticism (Zuhd). This hadith, found in al-Kafi’s chapter on love of the world, underscores that excessive attachment to physical appetites creates a veil that obscures divine proximity, urging believers to elevate their consciousness beyond mere biological survival.
